title: Finite affine-free syzygies of constructible etale modules
statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring, and let $F$ be a constructible sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. Set $K_0=F$. For every integer $r\geq1$, one can choose a finite family of affine etale objects $U_{r,t}$ of $X$ and an epimorphism $E_{r-1}=\bigoplus_t j_{U_{r,t}!}\Lambda_{U_{r,t}}\twoheadrightarrow K_{r-1}$ [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-module-finite-zero-cokernel], define $K_r=\ker(E_{r-1}\to K_{r-1})$, and obtain an exact sequence $0\to K_r\to E_{r-1}\to\cdots\to E_0\to F\to0$ in $\Mod(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Every $K_a$ is constructible.

source.place: Tag 095N (lemma-category-constructible-modules), finite affine-free presentations; Tag 03RZ (lemma-constructible-abelian), closure under kernels; Tag 03S8 (lemma-jshriek-constructible), constructibility of the finite affine-free summands. Finite iteration of these results.

proof.text: Fix r≥1 and argue by induction on a=0,…,r−1. The base K₀=F is constructible by hypothesis. If Kₐ is constructible, apply [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-module-finite-zero-cokernel] with the same qcqs scheme X and finite commutative ring Λ. It supplies finitely many affine étale objects U_{a+1,t} and a morphism from the coproduct of the corresponding sheafifications P_{U_{a+1,t}} of the free Λ-module presheaves V↦Λ^{(Hom_X(V,U_{a+1,t}))} onto Kₐ whose cokernel is zero. By [lem-weil-pbc-free-etale-module-shriek-comparison] (no hypothesis on W or Λ), each P_{U_{a+1,t}} is isomorphic to j_{U_{a+1,t}!}Λ_{U_{a+1,t}}, the étale extension by zero of [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension]; composing with these isomorphisms, call the finite direct sum Eₐ=⊕_t j_{U_{a+1,t}!}Λ_{U_{a+1,t}} and its map eₐ:Eₐ→Kₐ, which still has zero cokernel. In the abelian category [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], zero cokernel makes eₐ an epimorphism, so its kernel K_{a+1}=ker(eₐ) exists. Each U_{a+1,t} is affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and étale over the qcqs scheme X, so [lem-weil-pbc-etale-free-sheaf-constructible] with M=Λ shows that each summand j_{U_{a+1,t}!}Λ_{U_{a+1,t}} is constructible (Stacks 03S8 (3)). A finite direct sum of constructible sheaves is constructible by the extension clause (2) of [thm-constructible-serre], applied to the split short exact sequences 0→G→G⊕G'→G'→0 and induction on the number of summands; the empty sum 0=Ker(id_{Kₐ}) is constructible by clause (1). So eₐ is a morphism between constructible sheaves, and the kernel clause (1) of [thm-constructible-serre] shows K_{a+1} is constructible, completing the induction step.

proof.text: For each a<r, the kernel definition and the epimorphism eₐ give a short exact sequence 0→K_{a+1}→Eₐ→Kₐ→0. Define the map Eₐ→E_{a−1} as Eₐ→Kₐ followed by the kernel inclusion Kₐ→E_{a−1}; consecutive composites are zero. At Eₐ, the image of E_{a+1}→Eₐ is K_{a+1}, because E_{a+1}→K_{a+1} is epi, while the kernel of Eₐ→Kₐ is exactly K_{a+1}; at the last term the same assertion is the kernel definition. At Kₐ the incoming map is epi and the outgoing kernel inclusion is monic. Thus finite splicing gives 0→Kᵣ→E_{r−1}→⋯→E₀→F→0 in Mod(X_et,Λ), and the induction gives constructibility of every Kₐ.

split_report.summary: Split the finite affine-free syzygy construction into the inductive finite affine epimorphism/kernel step and the elementary finite splicing step. The induction uses the existing Tag 095N finite affine epimorphism node, identifies its sheafification with j_!Λ via the existing extension-by-zero definition, and applies the existing weak-Serre kernel closure theorem from Tag 03RZ. No new DAG nodes were needed. Maintainer review (Q52 reader, 2026-10-18): step 1 now cites lem-weil-pbc-free-etale-module-shriek-comparison for P_U ≅ j_{U!}Λ_U (the extension-by-zero definition alone does not state it) and lem-weil-pbc-etale-free-sheaf-constructible plus the extension clause of thm-constructible-serre for constructibility of E_a, which the kernel clause needs; thm-constructible-serre removed from stmt_deps since the statement does not use it.

lean.statement: theorem exists_constructible_etale_finite_affine_syzygy (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ] [Finite Λ] (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)) (hF : IsConstructibleEtaleModuleSheaf F) (r : ℕ) (hr : 1 ≤ r) : ∃ (K : Fin (r + 1) → Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)) (E : Fin r → Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)) (n : Fin r → ℕ) (U : ∀ a : Fin r, Fin (n a) → X.Etale) (i : ∀ a : Fin r, K a.succ ⟶ E a) (e : ∀ a : Fin r, E a ⟶ K a.castSucc), K 0 = F ∧ (∀ a : Fin (r + 1), IsConstructibleEtaleModuleSheaf (K a)) ∧ (∀ (a : Fin r) (t : Fin (n a)), IsAffine (U a t).left) ∧ (∀ a : Fin r, E a = ∐ fun t : Fin (n a) ↦ (Etale.etaleLowerShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) (U a t).hom inferInstance).obj ((constantSheaf (U a t).left.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)).obj (ModuleCat.of Λ Λ))) ∧ ∃ w : ∀ a : Fin r, i a ≫ e a = 0, ∀ a : Fin r, (ShortComplex.mk (i a) (e a) (w a)).ShortExact
